lit-violet.purpose: The readable member of the ramp. All accent text, in both themes.

room-black.purpose: The page. The dark room itself.

bench-navy.purpose: Panels and cards — the surface work is laid on.

riser-navy.purpose: Raised fills, chips, hover states, input grounds.

reading-grey.purpose: Secondary prose meant to be read — subtitles, descriptions.

quiet-grey.purpose: Labels, timestamps, hints. Present, not competing.

bloom-violet.purpose: The stop between Signal Violet and Lit Violet; carries the horizon bloom and sits inside both arc gradients.

display.purpose: Marketing headlines only. Never inside the app.

headline.purpose: The one page-owning h1 — a greeting, a brand's name on its plate.

label.purpose: Uppercase section eyebrows and meta keys.

arabic.purpose: A separate stack at 1.85 leading, not a fallback.

gradients.name: brand-gradient
gradients.purpose: The primary control fill and the lit edge source. One per view. Vertical and value-graded rather than a 135deg hue sweep: the light in this system is below the content, so the fill is brightest along its bottom edge. Every stop carries a 14px white label — 5.44:1 at the violet bottom, 7.00:1 in the middle, 9.47:1 at the deep blue top.

gradients.name: lit-edge
gradients.value: linear-gradient(0deg, color-mix(in srgb, #7240ff 34%, transparent), color-mix(in srgb, #ffffff 4%, transparent) 38%)
gradients.purpose: The hairline on what matters, lit along its bottom edge by the arc rising behind the fold.

gradients.name: horizon-arc
gradients.purpose: The rim across the hero's arc. Its named stops read the tokens at the source so a re-anchored ramp moves the arc with it; the pale stops between them are samples along that ramp rather than palette members.

gradients.name: section-arc
gradients.purpose: The same light further away: thinner, dimmer, rising from a section base.

gradients.name: horizon-bloom
gradients.purpose: The haze the crest throws up into the copy above it.

gradients.name: horizon-body
gradients.purpose: The lit band under the rim. The reference carries eighty-odd pixels of colour below its rim before the disc goes dark, and that band is most of what makes the arc read as an object with light behind it rather than as a drawn line.

shadows.name: soft
shadows.purpose: The resting state of any raised surface.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Hover and active elevation. The indigo tint is what makes it read as light rather than darkness.

shadows.name: glow-brand
shadows.value: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, #7240ff 25%, transparent), 0 0 24px -4px color-mix(in srgb, #7240ff 55%, transparent), 0 0 64px -8px color-mix(in srgb, #7240ff 38%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: The brand-carrying moment. Both blur layers centred rather than offset downward: measured off the reference, this is a light with a halo, not a raised box.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Field focus. A bloom outside the border, not an outline.

motion.name: ease-out-soft
motion.purpose: Entrances and all default state transitions.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Scale-in, where a small overshoot reads as arrival.

motion.name: duration-band
motion.purpose: Interface motion. Outside this band it reads as decorative rather than responsive.

motion.name: stagger-step
motion.purpose: List entrances via a --i index; the cap stops a long list leaving its last row waiting.

narrative.overview:
The interface is the dark room. Every brand this product generates is a print that comes out of it, and the print is the only thing carrying colour. That is why the chrome sits at near-black and holds a single accent ramp: it is not minimalism as a style preference, it is a room built so that whatever is pinned up in it can be judged. A product that sells brand coherence cannot show a customer's brand inside its own purple and expect to be believed.

So the register is a quiet instrument around loud work. Chrome is severe: hairline edges mixed from white rather than drawn in grey, three tonal grounds instead of borders, one accent that appears where something means something. Expression is delegated outward — a project page adopts the palette and the faces of the brand it is showing, and Brandora's own ramp withdraws to the shell. The one place the chrome is allowed to be expressive is motion, and even there it is bounded: nothing loops forever except a running job and a loading skeleton.

The visual anti-reference is the admin template — same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text, figures that restate a count nobody asked for, and a grey 1px border around everything. Those were all present and all removed deliberately; a change that reintroduces them is a regression regardless of how it looks in isolation.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black navy ground with three tonal steps, never a grey border
One accent ramp, violet through blue, used sparingly and never as text at full strength
Light from above: a gradient top edge on what matters, brand-tinted shadow below
The generated brand owns any region that displays it, with contrast guarded at runtime
Generous radii (14 / 20 / 24px) and a 150–300ms motion band that collapses entirely under reduced-motion
Fully bilingual: every surface works in Arabic with RTL, on its own font stack

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: There is no second accent. Status colours aside, anything that needs emphasis borrows from Signal Violet, Indigo Core or Horizon Blue. A new colour entering the system is a design decision, not an implementation detail.

rules.name: The Readable Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Violet is 3.4:1 on Room Black — enough under a button, not enough under words. Accent text is always Lit Violet, which clears 7:1 in both themes. This is why the two values differ per theme while the ramp does not.

rules.name: The Checked Tone Rule
rules.body: Every colour this system puts under text is verified against its own ground, not assumed from a percentage. A color-mix at 42% of its own background cannot reach 4.5:1 for any pair of colours in existence — that is arithmetic, not a data problem — so guest-brand text tones are resolved by stepping the mix until it clears the floor.

rules.name: The Guest Palette Rule
rules.body: On any surface displaying a generated brand, that brand's palette owns the region and Brandora's ramp withdraws to the shell. The guest palette is untrusted input: every colour that ends up under text is contrast-checked at runtime and replaced when it fails, so a bad generation degrades to plain rather than to unreadable. Secondary text on a guest ground is mixed from that brand's own ink, never set to grey.

rules.name: The Rendered Light Rule
rules.body: The horizon arcs and their bloom are light, not surfaces, so they interpolate across the ramp and through white rather than stepping between named swatches. Their intermediate stops — pale violets, pale blues, a white core — are samples along that ramp and belong to the gradient definitions in the sidecar, not to the palette. Anything that is not rendered light uses a named colour.

rules.name: The Word-Not-Letter Rule
rules.body: Headline motion splits on words, never on characters. Character-level animation reads as a typewriter gimmick at display size and it breaks Arabic outright, where letterforms join.

rules.name: The Tracking Floor Rule
rules.body: Negative tracking scales with size: -0.02em at title, -0.03em at headline, -0.035em at display, and never past -0.04em.

rules.name: The No Dead Column Rule
rules.body: A persistent side region must earn its width down the whole page. A rail holding four links above a screen-height of nothing is the failure this system was rebuilt to remove; give it more to hold, or let it collapse.

rules.name: The Light From Above Rule
rules.body: Illumination enters at the top edge. A uniform 1px outline on all four sides is what made this app read as a template beside its own marketing; the lit edge replaced it and should not be reintroduced.

rules.name: The Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: No shadow in this system is pure black. Tint with the ground's navy for weight, with Indigo Core for lift.

rules.name: The Measured Figure Rule
rules.body: A figure earns its tile by being measurable. Every series is bucketed from a real timestamp; where the data cannot support a trend the tile shows none rather than a decorative line; a level takes no percentage, because the denominator is whatever the account happened to hold at an arbitrary earlier moment; and a metric with no good direction says so rather than colouring itself green or red. This replaced the outright ban on a row of stat tiles, which was lifted after three dashboards were built and measured — the tiles started 50px lower than the contact sheet and still put six brands in the fold against its two.

dos: Do delegate colour outward on any surface showing a generated brand, and contrast-check every guest colour that ends up under text.
Do use Lit Violet (#aa8cff / #5b33cc) for accent text and Signal Violet (#7240ff) for fills. They are not interchangeable.
Do mix borders from white at 9% or 16% into the ground rather than drawing a grey line.
Do put a lit gradient edge on what matters and a plain hairline on what does not.
Do pick the radius by role: 14px to operate, 20px for a card, 24px for a panel of cards.
Do keep interface motion in the 150–300ms band, ease entrances out and exits in, and collapse all of it under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do design both directions. Arabic uses its own stack at 1.85 leading, and every layout uses logical properties.
donts: Don't clip the brand gradient to text. It was removed for legibility: part of every glyph sits on the lowest-contrast stop, and the words vanish entirely where the clip is unsupported.
Don't introduce a second accent colour, or a solid grey 1px border, or a shadow made of pure black.
Don't nest a card inside a card. Drop the inner one to a plain region with a hairline rule.
Don't build a page as a stack of same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text. That one stands.
Don't show a figure this system cannot measure — no invented trend, no percentage on a level, no delta against a period nobody named. See the Measured Figure Rule.
Don't leave a persistent side rail holding less than a screen of content — give it more or let it collapse.
Don't animate headlines letter by letter; split on words, because Arabic letterforms join.
Don't signal a state with colour alone; the word rides with the dot.
